title: Introduce lint signal router and minimal release transaction
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: Presubmit latency spikes and noisy reruns from monolithic lint/test lanes make PR feedback slow for mid-size changes. This PR introduces a lightweight "lint signal router" that routes files changed to targeted lint executors and a minimal "release transaction" abstraction so release hooks can be decoupled and orchestrated without long-lived top-level scripts. Goals: reduce presubmit CI time for common change types, reduce wasted test matrix runs, and make release automation composable and auditable. Design summary: 1) lint-signal-router: inspects changed paths and emits a compact signal (json payload) that maps to lint profiles (ts, python, go, infra) and suggested presubmit lanes. Router is intentionally hermetic and runs as a fast pre-check in the presubmit runner; it does not replace existing lint rules but gates which lint shards run in the expensive runner. 2) release-transaction: a small orchestrator (Go) that sequences release steps (build, sign, publish, tag) as a transactional set with explicit checkpoints and compensating rollback hooks. It provides a dry-run mode for CI and an audit trail (event log) for postmortems. Rollout plan: feature branch + opt-in CI flag for 7 days, then flip default in staged lanes; will gradually add more mappings to lint-signal-router over two sprints. Checklist: - [x] lint router proto and tests - [x] minimal mapping for ts/python/go/infra - [x] release-transaction dry-run in nightly - [x] docs and runbook - [x] rollout flag gated behind experiment config Risks and mitigations: - Missing file globs might under-run linters: router has a conservative fallback that triggers full lint on unknown paths. - Release transaction failure during publish: we add compensating rollback hooks and a safe-mode that pauses and alerts to SRE. Related: builds on prior presubmit-slimline work (ENG-1021) and addresses SUP-4091 customer report of noisy releases. Implementation notes: commits are small, each focuses on a single area—router, mappings, release tx, docs, and test harness. The router binary is ~650 LOC; release transaction ~900 LOC with unit tests and an integration smoke harness that runs in CI using ephemeral test buckets. How to review: focus on mapping rules (configs under .ci/mappings) and the release transaction's checkpoint semantics. The PR also includes a small CLI shim used by release automation to call release-transaction with proper credentials. Links: linear:ENG-1248, ENG-1312; support ticket: SUP-4091. Rollback: revert feature flag and run full presubmit on the affected PRs if we see regression.

diff_snippets:
--- a/.ci/runner/presubmit_runner.go
+++ b/.ci/runner/presubmit_runner.go
@@ -120,6 +120,22 @@ func runPresubmit(...) {
+    // early lint routing: fast signal generation to avoid running full lint matrix
+    if cfg.EnableLintSignalRouter {
+        sig := router.EmitSignal(changedPaths)
+        lanes := mappings.SelectLanes(sig)
+        executor.RunLanes(lanes)
+        return
+    }

    // existing expensive path...
--- a/tools/release-transaction/txn/checkpoints.go
+++ b/tools/release-transaction/txn/checkpoints.go
@@ -1,6 +1,28 @@
+// checkpoint: record and emit an audit event for each completed step
+func (t *Transaction) recordCheckpoint(step string, meta map[string]string) error {
+    t.log.Emit(Event{Step: step, Meta: meta})
+    return nil
+}

+// compensating rollback example: delete published artifact on failure
+func (t *Transaction) rollbackPublish(ctx context.Context) error {
+    // best-effort, idempotent cleanup
+    return t.storage.DeleteArtifact(ctx, t.lastArtifactID)
+}
--- a/.ci/mappings/default_mappings.yaml
+++ b/.ci/mappings/default_mappings.yaml
@@
 - pattern: "**/*.ts"
   lanes: ["lint-ts", "unit-ts"]
 - pattern: "**/*.py"
   lanes: ["lint-py", "unit-py"]
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice separation. Two asks: (1) can we make the router config hot-reloadable so we don't need a full runner deploy to tweak mappings? (2) add a conservative integration test that simulates a monorepo change set.
Asha Menon: @Diego added hot-reload support to mappings via a filewatch in the router and a test that exercises 3 change set variants. See commit b3e2f44.
Maya Patel: The release-transaction looks good but please ensure we redact secrets from the audit event log. Also prefer retries with exponential backoff instead of fixed sleeps.
Asha Menon: @Maya added scrubbing of tokens in events and switched to backoff.Retry with capped jitter (commit d5b2aee).

Tomoko Saito: CI flakes in the first run: router smoke test failed due to ephemeral bucket permission misconfiguration. Reran and passed. Please add a note in the runbook about ephemeral bucket creation rights.
Asha Menon: Updated runbook and made the ephemeral bucket creation explicit in scripts (commit f7c1aa4).
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals. Small rework based on reviewer feedback: added hot-reload for mappings, token scrubbing, and runbook updates. Dry-run validated in nightly jobs.
release_notes: Introduce lint-signal-router to reduce presubmit feedback time by routing changed files to targeted lint lanes. Add release-transaction orchestrator to provide transactional release steps with dry-run and audit logging. Opt-in feature flag for two weeks, then enabled by default.
notes_for_ops: If you see presubmit regressions enable PRESUBMIT_FULL_MATRIX=true in CI config to revert to existing behavior. Release transaction failures will emit an alert to #release-ops; use txnctl inspect <run_id> for audit events.
tests_added: unit tests for router/mappings, integration smoke tests for router and release txn, nightly dry-run coverage
review_flow: Approved by Diego Alvarez (code), Maya Patel (security/perf), Tomoko Saito (sre). One CI re-run after ephemeral infra fix. Merged via squash after final green CI.
